A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L-Cross Modulation study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-model steering experiments, ablations, generalization analyses, and weak-to-strong results in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–4 and the supplementary experimental figures.

M1.justification: CAA/RepE steering-vector extraction, ordinary-least-squares alignment, and scaled vector addition to target-model hidden states remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven CAA and four RepE concepts, including the same AdvBench harmfulness questions and fairness and emotion scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain No Modulation, Self Modulation, and the same source-model comparisons. The no-transformation and random-transformation ablation variants are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, 50-question/output evaluations, metrics, evaluation prompts, layer choices, and modulation-strength settings remain unchanged across Section 4 and Appendices A–E.

E4.justification: The transformation ablations, t-SNE visualization, matrix-similarity analysis, modulation-strength sweeps, qualitative example, and supplementary weak-to-strong experiments are retained. The added discussion introduces no additional analysis or controlled test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing point estimates and curve-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. Section 4.2 newly describes qualitative patterns: cross-model improvements usually accompany self-modulation improvements, and Qwen2–Llama3.1 and Llama2–Llama3.1 pairings often perform better.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, least-squares formulation and pseudoinverse solution, and transfer equation in Sections 2–3 remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: linear cross-model transfer, generalization across concepts, and weak-to-strong steering.

C2.justification: The new Section 4.2 paragraph interprets model-pair performance as indicating better representation alignment for models with closer release dates or shared architectures. This explanation is not separately tested; the existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B changes the GPT-4o mini reference hyperlink, introducing literal backslashes into its target. Hardware, implementation instructions, hyperparameters, evaluation prompts, and code/data links otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged, including distinctions from soft-prompt transfer and transferable jailbreaking research.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short discussion paragraph and an Acknowledgments section, updates affiliation/contact information, and makes a small wording edit to RQ1. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All six tables and twelve figures retain their content. Figure 3 and appendix material are repositioned, printed page numbers disappear, and reflow leaves v2 PDF page 16 almost empty.

improvement.justification: The method, empirical support, and limitations remain essentially identical. The added interpretation offers limited context without separately supporting its release-date/architecture explanation. Contact corrections and funding disclosure provide small benefits, while the malformed evaluator link and sparse appendix page reduce polish; these changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
